solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Scot's exam covering state of Germany

indicators.note: the exam word goes round, or covers, the German state word

parts.note: a Higher is the Scottish school-leaving exam
a Land is one of the federal states of Germany

explanation.surface: A Scottish pupil sits an exam that happens to cover one of Germany's states.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGHERS are the exams Scottish pupils sit at about seventeen; a German federal state is a LAND (plural Länder).
explanation.definitionFit: A Highlander is a native of the Scottish Highlands, so certainly a Scot.

clue.text: Restrain worker on strike

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand
to cuff is to strike with the open hand

explanation.surface: A worker who has gone on strike is being held back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on strike' reads as industrial action, but 'on' only places the worker above the blow.
explanation.definitionFit: To put cuffs on someone's wrists is to physically restrain them.

clue.text: Soldier's turn with vulgar-sounding escort

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
a go is a turn, as in 'your go'

indicators.note: the word for vulgar is heard, not written, here

parts.note: low means coarse or vulgar

explanation.surface: A soldier takes his turn with a crude escort.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man paid to accompany and entertain a woman, a hired escort.

clue.text: Rope in the Parisian — number left laughing

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)

indicators.note: left here means departed, so the number letter goes out of the word for laughing

parts.note: riant is a literary word for laughing or cheerful

explanation.surface: Someone in Paris is roped in to a show that leaves a crowd laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: RIANT (laughing, from French) loses N, leaving RIAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a long noosed rope used by cowboys.

clue.text: Male youth who could be a miss?

definitions.text: Male youth who could be a miss?

parts.words: Male youth who could be a miss?
parts.note: a male youth is almost a man, and one who is always almost there is a near miss of a man

explanation.surface: A boy who might be mistaken for a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'miss' looks like a girl but is a near miss; the phrase names someone who repeatedly falls just short of success.
explanation.definitionFit: A youth is not yet fully grown, so he is almost a man; the idiom means a perennial runner-up.

clue.text: More than fifty will get access to area code

indicators.note: the number gets into, gains entry to, the area word

parts.note: a region is an area
LI is 51 in Roman numerals, one more than fifty

explanation.surface: A rule that anyone over fifty may enter a zone with a particular dialling code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'area code' looks like a phone prefix but splits into wordplay and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A religion is a system of belief and moral rules, a code to live by.

clue.text: Ambassador assuming work may be long

indicators.note: to assume is to take on, so the envoy's letters take the work word inside

parts.note: HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador
op (opus) is a musical work

explanation.surface: An ambassador taking on a job that may drag on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are verbs of yearning: to long for something is to wish or desire for it.

clue.text: Bit of a laugh before unknown excitement causes snitch irritation

indicators.note: the laugh piece comes first

parts.note: ha is one burst of laughter
y is an algebraic unknown
fever is a state of excitement, as in fever pitch

explanation.surface: A joke followed by a mysterious agitation leads to an annoying informer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snitch' looks like an informer; it is old slang for the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollen allergy inflames the nasal passages, so the condition is an irritation of the nose.

clue.text: Relating to meal Dan and April prepared

indicators.note: food that is prepared is made ready, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Dan and April are cooking dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective comes from Latin prandium, lunch, and describes anything to do with a meal.

clue.text: African spirit returns, meeting Queen in a novel

indicators.note: the spirit word comes back, read from the end

parts.note: gin is a spirit
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

indicators.note: novel means new, so the two little words are made new by rearranging

explanation.surface: An African spirit turns up beside a queen in a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns GIN into NIG; 'novel' rearranges IN A into IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nigerian is a person from Nigeria, a country of West Africa.

clue.text: Amateur songster?

definitions.meaning: a non-professional, someone without expert training
a lay is a song or ballad, so a singer of lays might whimsically be called this

explanation.surface: An amateur singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone untrained in a profession is lay; a lay is also an old poem or song.

clue.text: To blame clue is misguided — it's about record by Jack

indicators.note: the scrambled clue word goes round the record and sailor
misguided means led astray, so the letters of clue go wrong
by means beside, so the sailor follows the record

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, and AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: A setter admits a misleading clue is about a record by someone named Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misguided' rearranges CLUE into CU...LE, which goes 'about' LPAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone culpable deserves blame, being guilty or at fault.

clue.text: Voracious journalist in dull surroundings

indicators.note: the colour word surrounds the journalist

parts.note: grey means dull or dreary
ed, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A hungry reporter in drab surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe an excessive appetite for food or wealth.

clue.text: Record will be playing in little while

indicators.note: the playing word goes into the little while

parts.note: mo is short for moment
on means playing, as a record is on

explanation.surface: The record will start in a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A mono is a monophonic recording, one made on a single channel.

clue.text: French church remote and ornate

indicators.note: ornate means elaborately decorated, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

explanation.surface: A French church that is remote and lavishly decorated.
explanation.definitionFit: The cathedral of Notre-Dame stands on the Île de la Cité in Paris.

clue.text: Doctor's admitted favouring South Africa's old detached area

indicators.note: the doctor is let in between the other pieces

parts.note: for means in favour of
SA is the abbreviation for South Africa
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor admits he favours an old breakaway region of South Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Formosa is the old name of Taiwan, an island separated from mainland China.

clue.text: Tenant put pound initially into different account

indicators.note: the pound letter goes into the rearranged account
different means changed, so account's letters are reordered
only the first letter of pound is taken

explanation.surface: A renter pays a pound into a new bank account.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupant lives in a property, as a tenant does.

clue.text: Very small details, two different ones appearing in time

indicators.note: the two ones show up inside the time word

parts.note: a minute is a measure of time
I (Roman numeral) and A (as in a single thing) are two different ways of writing one

explanation.surface: Fine details of two separate items appear in the timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Minutiae are trivial particulars, the fine points of something.

clue.text: Take away vehicle over land

indicators.note: in a down clue the vehicle sits over the land

parts.note: a sub, submarine, is an underwater vessel
a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: Remove a vehicle across country.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to deduct or take one number from another.

clue.text: American's in a submarine, maybe, enjoying life?

definitions.meaning: a submarine is a long sandwich in the US, so a filling is placed in bread
having a run of success, everything going well

explanation.surface: An American aboard a submarine is having a good time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'submarine' looks naval, but in American English it is also a long bread sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a winning streak, and literally describes something placed in bread.

clue.text: Beans Lee served up for people in the country

indicators.note: food served up is presented anew, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Lee serves beans to country folk.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lebanese are the people of Lebanon, the Middle Eastern country.

clue.text: One continuing to hold it back

indicators.note: the held letters run backwards
the word continuing holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: One who keeps holding on to something behind them.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single thing, a quantity of one.

clue.text: Nonconformist padre acquires university study

indicators.note: the rearranged padre takes in the university letter
nonconformist means not keeping to the usual order, so the letters of padre are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dissenting chaplain enrols at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nonconformist' looks like a Protestant church label, but it rearranges PADRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To read up on a subject is to study it thoroughly.

clue.text: Mark of corporal (punishment)

definitions.meaning: a corporal wears two chevrons on the sleeve as rank insignia
a lash or stroke of the whip given as a penalty

explanation.surface: A soldier bearing the scars of corporal punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket hides the phrase 'corporal punishment', which joins the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a rank chevron on a uniform and a single stroke of a whip.

clue.text: Summer term when Masters course is cut short

indicators.note: the last letter is cut off the golf course's name

parts.note: Augusta National in Georgia hosts the Masters golf tournament

explanation.surface: A school term that falls when a master's degree course is shortened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Masters' looks academic, but it is the golf tournament.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth month is a summer period in the northern hemisphere.

clue.text: Refasten broken window

indicators.note: broken means smashed into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Secure a smashed window again.
explanation.definitionFit: Fenestra is Latin for window, used for a small opening in anatomy or architecture.

clue.text: Woman or a man in sporting alliance

indicators.note: a and the man go inside the sporting body

parts.note: the FA is the Football Association
Tim is a man's name

explanation.surface: Either a woman or a man may belong to a sports association.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatima is a woman's name, after the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: Tough had jumped right queue

indicators.note: letters that jump move out of place, so they are rearranged

parts.note: a line is a queue of people

explanation.surface: A tough customer pushed straight to the front of the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumped' rearranges HAD with R into HARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardline stance is uncompromising and strict, a tough one.

clue.text: Reported dirty place that's an eyesore?

indicators.note: reported means spoken of, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, a filthy place

explanation.surface: A filthy place has been reported as an eyesore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eyesore' is taken literally: a sore on the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, literally a sore on the eye.

clue.text: Suit(e)

parts.note: the bracketed letter lets the clue read as a suit of clothes or a suite of furniture, both of which come in a three-part version

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a jacket, trousers and waistcoat outfit, and a sofa with two matching armchairs.
